contradicting_evidence: An upside edge is plausible: BTC and ETH gained about 1.40% and 1.81% over 24h, while the freshest breadth proxy shows 68 of 100 constituents advancing.
A downside edge is also plausible: BTC hourly taker-buy quote share was 41.35%, and the sampled BTC and ETH order books were ask-heavy.
The latest settled ETF session recorded BTC outflows of $398.6 million and ETH outflows of $139.7 million, although these are not contemporaneous intraday flows.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: Immediate direction is unresolved. Brief stabilization or a renewed rebound is credible, but so is another test lower. The supplied evidence does not support an ordering of those moves or a reliable net 12h direction; NO_EDGE is not a forecast of a narrow range.
falsification_conditions: Repeated completed-hour gains with persistent spot buying, stronger ETH/BTC and maintained broad participation would replace the no-edge assessment with an upside case.
Repeated completed-hour losses accompanied by weakening participation and persistent aggressive selling would establish a downside case.
missing_evidence: A multi-hour sequence showing whether current participation and buying pressure persist.
Persistent, multi-venue order-flow confirmation rather than one depth and trade snapshot.
supporting_evidence: The positive 24h backdrop conflicts with slightly negative latest hourly returns: BTC approximately -0.03%, ETH -0.06% and ETH/BTC -0.03%.
BTC and ETH open interest declined modestly alongside price. This shows some exposure reduction, not confirmed recovery or an expanding fresh-short trend.
Spot-flow measures are inconsistent across sampling windows: the BTC trade snapshot is slightly buy-positive, but its completed-hour taker-buy share is below half.
